title: Reuse imported verification with full source currency and terminal conflict accounting
outcome: Supported imported verification can satisfy existing destination requirements through common local applicability and full source equality, while contradictory terminal facts remain visible and cannot earn new destination credit.
acceptance: An explicit local association/ordinary completion selection consumes supported imported registered or remote verification through the common qualifier and actual destination governing/run/root/claim basis. Equal complete clean and dirty SourceId values qualify under existing rules; commit/tree/changes/submodule drift, an unmatched Git carrier commit and failed aggregate do not. No import timestamp rejuvenation or new host/environment/rerun condition is added.

The keyed execution union includes supported authoritative terminal bodies in both original terminal-origin and association request records, including ResultConflict/refused associations. Tests deliver equivalent different-id and conflicting same-/cross-store records in both orders, including PASS origin P followed by FAIL association A still linking P; new conflict invalidates dependent current unconsumed eligibility atomically, original refusals/credit/seals stay unchanged and one execution is not counted twice.

Reported gates, observation-embedded uncredited checks, unsupported/provisional bodies and malformed/incomplete provenance never become observed verification. Exact original bytes, results, execution times and host provenance remain unchanged; a new local applicability decision has its own identity and distinguishes origin assurance from local observation.

Active local governing/runtime mutations remain held until normal release/completion/lapse; passive history does not require TermAl or drain. Behavioral tests cover bound/unbound requirements, no-op/reverse replay, stale local source, late conflicts and transaction rollback with no partial satisfaction; display stays bounded and docs describe supported reuse.
